title: Tea From Both Hands
logline: A village shopkeeper has given the same regular customer something small every day for years. Some days it's more, some days it's less, and neither of them has ever said why.
human_question: When the same person gives you the same kind of thing every day, what actually changes from one day to the next?

premise.story: The daily exchange between a shopkeeper and a regular customer over several weeks, tracking the small variations in what is given.
premise.place: A small village shop, a counter worn smooth by decades of hands.
premise.experience: Watching an ordinary transaction closely enough to see that it is never quite the same twice.

concept_links.why: The Margaya's own example is one giver and one recipient, the same kind of mind on different days, where the strength of intention differs from a coin to a note [C011-M:L26].
Ordinary capacities like attention and effort take on the colour of the moment they serve, which is why the same daily act never looks quite identical [C019-P:L61-L63].

what_camera_could_observe: The counter, and whatever passes for a ledger or memory of who is owed what
Small, real variations in what is given from one day to the next
Conversation between the two of them building over weeks
The shopkeeper's own account of the customer, and the customer's of the shopkeeper
what_must_be_real: The shopkeeper's and customer's actual relationship and reasons. The recipient must be a full, consenting participant, never a symbol of need.

possible_arc.opening: An ordinary transaction at the counter, early in the day.
possible_arc.turn: A day when noticeably more, or less, is given, and why, if either of them will say.
possible_arc.ending_open: What the two of them actually say to each other, or to Chathura, when finally asked directly.

position_hint: opening candidate: a real, ordinary act of free giving that could plausibly be where Object 6 changes hands, only if it happens naturally

requirements: A shopkeeper and a regular customer with a long, real relationship willing to be filmed
Enough filming time to observe genuine day-to-day variation, not one staged exchange
The recipient's full, informed consent and comfort with the camera

suggestions.name: A small shop in a hill-country or Sabaragamuwa village
suggestions.why: Small village shops with long-standing regular customers are common across this region.
suggestions.verify: No specific shop, shopkeeper or customer has been identified.

risks: Exposing the recipient's need or hardship for the camera
Turning a private, decades-long relationship into a demonstration
Implying the size of a gift measures the giver's worth, which the source explicitly does not claim
drop_if: The recipient does not want to be filmed, or the relationship turns out to be arranged rather than long-standing

connections.note: Both are ordinary, repeated acts of free giving to someone who cannot reciprocate, and both are candidates for where Object 6 first changes hands.
Both watch the same kind of giving become easier, or simply different, with repetition over time.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
